title: Bounded parse-and-compare run
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$. For every pair of Boolean words $p,s$ with $x=ps$, and every natural number $r$ at most the length of $c$’s output, the captured-length checker, started from the configuration built from $c$ with input head just past the prefix $p$, counter $r$, and its parser in the comparison phase, reaches a halted configuration within at most $|s|+1$ steps. Its output is the single bit $1$ exactly when the pair parser decodes $s$ as a pair whose second component has length at most $r$; otherwise its output is the single bit $0$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$x$ is a Boolean word and $c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $x$
$r$ is a natural number at most the length of $c$’s output
The running time is bounded by $|s|+1$ steps
replaced:
For a split $x = p s$ of the input and a counter $r$ at most the captured
word's length, from the checker's block-start parse state at position
$\abs{p}$ there is a time $t \le \abs{s} + 1$ after which the checker has
halted with a one-bit output: if $s$ decodes under the self-delimiting pair
code as $(a,b)$, the bit records whether $\abs{b} \le r$, and if $s$ is
malformed the bit is $0$.
